newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to clean Jakarta district of gangs.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to clean Jakarta district of gangs.

text.p: Indonesian police have pledged to rid the Tanah Abang shopping district in central Jakarta of hoodlums after a gang war last week, the Suara Pembaruan newspaper reported on Monday.
"We will clean the area of hoodlums," Jakarta police chief Major-General Hamami Nata was quoted as saying on Sunday.
He said the gangs had disturbed the peace in Tanah Abang, an important textile centre hemmed in by slums and brothels.
Shops in the district closed last Thursday after a turf war between two gangs. Residents said one gang consisted of East Timorese and the other Irianese.

At least 10 people were arrested for their alleged involvement in the incident. News of the disturbance spread quickly through Jakarta's financial markets, which have been jolted by recent riots and protests in Indonesia.
Nata said police would round up hoodlums from other areas, such as the Pasar Minggu bus terminal in South Jakarta where many public transport drivers had complained of extortion.
East Timorese sources said police and military officers had threatened to send Timorese youths in Tanah Abang back to the troubled territory after the gang war.
Many East Timorese youths had migrated to Jakarta under a job opportunity programme organised by a foundation chaired by President Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardijanti Rukmana.
